questions.q: What should you do first when the Regional Manager reports a reconciliation mismatch, before touching any table?
options: Reproduce it by re-running Lesson 9's exact reconciliation query against the specific store and day reported
Immediately re-run the MERGE job and hope it corrects itself
Drop and rebuild silver.sales_clean from scratch
Assume the Regional Manager misread the dashboard and close the ticket
questions.explain: Reproducing the issue with the existing validation tool turns a vague complaint into a concrete, confirmed discrepancy.

questions.q: For Store 48 on March 2nd, what did the reconciliation query show?
options: daily_sales_summary showed $15,342.18 while category_breakdown rolled up to $13,897.52 — a $1,444.66 gap
The two tables matched exactly, confirming there was no real problem
category_breakdown returned zero rows for that store and day
The gap was $0.01, within Lesson 9's normal rounding tolerance
questions.explain: A $1,444.66 gap is far outside Lesson 9's one-cent tolerance, confirming a genuine discrepancy rather than rounding noise.

questions.q: Why widen the reconciliation query to a date range instead of stopping after confirming one bad day?
options: Isolating the variable (the date) reveals exactly when the discrepancy starts, which narrows down the cause before you look for it
A wider date range is required by the Delta Lake engine to run the query at all
It has no diagnostic value; one bad day is always sufficient
To make gold.daily_sales_summary refresh faster
questions.explain: Changing one dimension (the date range) while holding the store constant shows precisely where the clean data ends and the broken data begins.

questions.q: What pattern did the widened query reveal for Store 48?
options: Every day before March 1st reconciled cleanly (diff = 0.00); every day from March 1st forward showed a nonzero diff
Every day, both before and after March 1st, showed the same $1,444.66 gap
The discrepancy appeared only on weekends
The discrepancy shrank over time and eventually disappeared on its own
questions.explain: A discrepancy that starts cleanly on one specific date and holds from there is the signature of a change that went live around that date, not random noise.

questions.q: What does this lesson explicitly say NOT to do yet?
options: Touch either Gold table or re-run the MERGE job hoping it fixes itself, before the real cause is confirmed
Run the reconciliation query for a specific store and day
Widen the query to a date range to look for a pattern
Write down the exact date the pattern changes
questions.explain: The lesson is about reproducing and isolating the symptom; confirming the actual cause is Lesson 14's job before anything changes.
